[![Looking at crowds down Broadway](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Broadway_Crowds_%285896264776%29_crop.jpg/250px-Broadway_Crowds_%285896264776%29_crop.jpg)](/wiki/File:Broadway_Crowds_(5896264776)_crop.jpg)

[Broadway](/wiki/Broadway_(Manhattan) "Broadway (Manhattan)") in [Midtown Manhattan](/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan "Midtown Manhattan"). As of the [2020 U.S. census](/wiki/2020_U.S._census "2020 U.S. census"), Manhattan was the most densely populated municipality in the United States.

As of the [2020 census](/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Manhattan's population had increased by 6.8% over the decade to 1,694,251, representing 19.2% of New York City's population of 8,804,190 and 8.4% of New York State's population of 20,201,249.[[5]](#cite_note-ManhattanQuickFacts-5) The population density of New York County was 70,450.8 inhabitants per square mile (27,201.2/km2) in 2022, the highest population density of any county in the United States and [higher than the density of any individual U.S. city](/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population_density#New_York_City_boroughs "List of United States cities by population density").[[171]](#cite_note-175)[[172]](#cite_note-176) At the [2010 census](/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"), there were 1,585,873 people living in Manhattan, an increase of 3.2% from the 1,537,195 counted in the [2000 census](/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census").[[173]](#cite_note-177)

The following is a list of mayors of [San Antonio, Texas](/wiki/San_Antonio,_Texas "San Antonio, Texas").

San Antonio operates under a [council–manager form of government](/wiki/Council%E2%80%93manager_government "Council–manager government").[[1]](#cite_note-Capps-1)[[2]](#cite_note-Navarro-2) While the mayor presides over meetings of the City Council and is paid $3,000 more than other members of the council, the mayor does not wield executive authority or [veto](/wiki/Veto "Veto") power. Rather, the mayor has one vote (of 11) on the city council, and the [city manager](/wiki/City_manager "City manager"), appointed by the City Council, has executive power (the city charter gives the manager the responsibility to "execute the laws and administer the government of the city").[[1]](#cite_note-Capps-1) However, the mayor does have additional ceremonial responsibilities, such as issuing proclamations. Additionally, the mayor is the only city-wide elected official, and "a high-profile mayor can wield considerable political influence" in the city.[[2]](#cite_note-Navarro-2) For example, the *[San Antonio Express-News](/wiki/San_Antonio_Express-News "San Antonio Express-News")* editorial board wrote that Mayor [Julian Castro](/wiki/Julian_Castro "Julian Castro") has "a mastery of political skill that made him a strong force in a weak mayor structure" during his term (2009–14).[[3

Artillery being landed during the invasion of mainland Italy at Salerno, September 1943

Forces of the British Eighth Army, still under Montgomery, landed in the 'toe' of Italy on 3 September 1943 in [Operation Baytown](/wiki/Operation_Baytown "Operation Baytown"), the day the Italian government agreed to [an armistice](/wiki/Armistice_of_Cassibile "Armistice of Cassibile") with the Allies. The armistice was publicly announced on 8 September by two broadcasts, first by General Eisenhower and then by a [proclamation by Marshal Badoglio](/wiki/Badoglio_Proclamation "Badoglio Proclamation"). Although the German forces prepared to defend without Italian assistance, only two of their divisions opposite the Eighth Army and one at [Salerno](/wiki/Salerno "Salerno") were not [tied up disarming](/wiki/Operation_Achse "Operation Achse") the [Royal Italian Army](/wiki/Royal_Italian_Army "Royal Italian Army").

On 9 September, forces of the [U.S. Fifth Army](/wiki/United_States_Army_North "United States Army North"), under Lieutenant General [Mark W. Clark](/wiki/Mark_W._Clark "Mark W. The [West Coast offense](/wiki/West_Coast_offense "West Coast offense") is the popular name for the high-percentage passing scheme designed by former Bengals assistant [Bill Walsh](/wiki/Bill_Walsh_(American_football_coach) "Bill Walsh (American football coach)").[[133]](#cite_note-m626-134) Walsh formulated what has become popularly known as the West Coast offense during his tenure as assistant coach for the Cincinnati Bengals from 1968 to 1975, while working under the tutelage of Brown (and before embarking on his legendary coaching tenure with the San Francisco 49ers in the 1980s). Bengals quarterback [Virgil Carter](/wiki/Virgil_Carter "Virgil Carter") was the first player to successfully implement Walsh's system, leading the NFL in pass completion percentage in 1971.[[134]](#cite_note-135) [Ken Anderson](/wiki/Ken_Anderson_(quarterback) "Ken Anderson (quarterback)") replaced Carter as Cincinnati's starting quarterback in 1972 and was even more successful. In 1975 he would bring widespread recognition to the West Coast offense as well as to the Cincinnati team and its quarterback in a nationally televised Monday night contest between the Bengals and a Buffalo Bills team built around the running game of star player [O. J. Simpson](/wiki/O._J._Simpson "O. J. Simpson"). Anderson's 447 passing yards were enough to overcome Simpson's 197 yards on the ground in a game that proved a milestone, providing a striking contrast between the "old" game of defense-minded football and the new game of higher scores and more action through a sophisticated aerial attack.[[135]](#cite_note-t055-136) The game, in effect, offered its viewers a glimpse of the future of professional football. **Sweden**,[[f]](#cite_note-15) formally the **Kingdom of Sweden**,[[g]](#cite_note-17)[[h]](#cite_note-18) is a [Nordic country](/wiki/Nordic_countries "Nordic countries") located on the [Scandinavian Peninsula](/wiki/Scandinavian_Peninsula "Scandinavian Peninsula") in [Northern Europe](/wiki/Northern_Europe "Northern Europe"). It borders [Norway](/wiki/Norway "Norway") to the west and north, and [Finland](/wiki/Finland "Finland") to the east, and shares a maritime border with [Denmark](/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") to the south. At 450,295 square kilometres (173,860 sq mi),[[4]](#cite_note-auto-7) Sweden is the largest Nordic country by both area and population, and is the [fifth-largest country in Europe](/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_area "List of European countries by area"). Its capital and largest city is [Stockholm](/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm"). Sweden has a population of 10.6 million, and a low population density of 25.5 inhabitants per square kilometre (66/sq mi); 88% of [Swedes](/wiki/Swedes "Swedes") reside in urban areas.[[11]](#cite_note-SCBdensity2020-19) They are mostly in the central and southern half of the country. Sweden's urban areas together cover 1.5% of its land area. Sweden has a diverse [climate](/wiki/Climate_of_Sweden "Climate of Sweden") owing to the length of the country, which ranges from [55°N](/wiki/55th_parallel_north "55th parallel north") to [69°N](/wiki/69th_parallel_north "69th parallel north").

Sweden has been inhabited since [prehistoric times](/wiki/Prehistoric_Sweden "Prehistoric Sweden") around 12,000 BC. The court has five male and four female justices. Among the nine justices, there are two [African American](/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans") justices (Justices [Thomas](/wiki/Clarence_Thomas "Clarence Thomas") and [Jackson](/wiki/Ketanji_Brown_Jackson "Ketanji Brown Jackson")) and one [Hispanic](/wiki/Hispanic "Hispanic") justice (Justice [Sotomayor](/wiki/Sonia_Sotomayor "Sonia Sotomayor")). One of the justices was born to at least one [immigrant](/wiki/Immigration "Immigration") parent: [Justice Alito](/wiki/Samuel_Alito "Samuel Alito")'s father was born in Italy.[[138]](#cite_note-138)[[139]](#cite_note-139)

At least six justices are [Roman Catholics](/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church"), one is [Jewish](/wiki/Judaism "Judaism"), and one is [Protestant](/wiki/Protestant "Protestant"). It is unclear whether [Neil Gorsuch](/wiki/Neil_Gorsuch "Neil Gorsuch") considers himself a Catholic or an [Episcopalian](/wiki/Episcopalian "Episcopalian").[[140]](#cite_note-gorsuchreligion-140) Historically, most justices have been Protestants, including 36 Episcopalians, 19 [Presbyterians](/wiki/Presbyterian "Presbyterian"), 10 [Unitarians](/wiki/Unitarianism "Unitarianism"), 5 [Methodists](/wiki/Methodist "Methodist"), and 3 [Baptists](/wiki/Baptists "Baptists").[[141]](#cite_note-141)[[142]](#cite_note-142) The first Catholic justice was [Roger Taney](/wiki/Roger_B._Taney "Roger B. Taney") in 1836,[[143]](#cite_note-143) and 1916 saw the appointment of the first Jewish justice, [Louis Brandeis](/wiki/Louis_Brandeis "Louis Brandeis").[[144]](#cite_note-SCOTUS_FAQ-144) In recent years the historical situation has reversed, as most recent justices have been either Catholic or Jewis
